# Cap-flat rounding without central symmetry: an exact planar source

Central symmetry of the entire source is not necessary for the
selected-group escape proved in
flat-symmetric-rounding-removes-free-simplex-compatibility.md.
Here is a concrete nonsymmetric three-fiber source with initially
active compatibility. Three finite reflections, one for each
selected cap normal, preserve its budgets through the preliminary
rounding and normalization. They also preserve the complete moving
threshold baseline needed for the joint Hessian argument.

The conclusion is a nearby compatible family with larger total
mass and all three selected cap masses strictly smaller. No
unselected budget or criticality of the selected cover is asserted.

## 1. Exact fibers and an active compatibility constraint

In R^2 put

    k0=(-1/3,-1/3), k1=(2/3,-1/3), k2=(-1/3,2/3),
    K=conv{k0,k1,k2},
    B=conv{b0,b1,b2},
    b0=(1,-1), b1=(0,1), b2=(-1,0).

At integer bases -1,0,1 take respectively

    K_-1=-K,  K_0=B,  K_1=K.                              (1)

The endpoint simplex has area V=1/2; B has area 3/2.
Thus M=5/2. The six vertices of (K-K)/2 are

    (1/2,0), (0,1/2), (-1/2,1/2),
    (-1/2,0), (0,-1/2), (1/2,-1/2).

The middle triangle has the exact facet description

    2x+y<=1,  -x+y<=1,  -x-2y<=1.                         (2)

All six displayed points satisfy (2), proving (K-K)/2 subset B.
The three points (1/2,0), (-1/2,1/2), (0,-1/2) lie respectively
on its three facets. Hence compatibility is active.

The convex hull of the three lifted fibers is a full-dimensional
convex body with exactly the stated three integer fibers.
The only excluded-target relation is the endpoint midpoint
relation at zero; every representation having middle selfweight
reduces to it.

The selected endpoint is not freely variable before strictification.
For example, translating K at base 1 a positive small distance in
the direction (2,1) moves the endpoint midpoint past the first
active facet of B while the other fibers stay fixed.

The source is not centrally symmetric: the base endpoints force
a possible symmetry center to have base zero, and the endpoint
pair forces continuous center zero. But -b0=(-1,1) violates the
second inequality in (2), so B is not centrally symmetric.

## 2. Three reflections and one invariant ellipsoid

The barycentric linear parts of K are

    l0(x,y)=-x-y, l1(x,y)=x, l2(x,y)=y,
    lambda_i=l_i+1/3.

Define the three linear involutions

    R0(x,y)=(-y,-x),
    R1(x,y)=(-x,x+y),
    R2(x,y)=(x+y,-y).                                      (3)

Each has determinant -1. It permutes the three vertices of B,
fixing one and swapping the other two. It also satisfies

    l_i(R_i x)=-l_i(x).                                    (4)

All three preserve the quadratic form x^2+xy+y^2. Consequently
the centrally symmetric ellipsoid

    E={(x,y): x^2+xy+y^2<=1}                               (5)

is invariant under every R_i. These facts follow directly from
(3), without a classification of reflection groups.

For every epsilon>=0 the body B+2epsilon E is invariant under
R_i. By (4), this determinant-one-in-absolute-value involution
exchanges its two l_i halfspaces. The cutting line has zero
area. Therefore

    |(B+2epsilon E) intersect {l_i>=0}|
       = |B+2epsilon E|/2,  i=0,1,2.                      (6)

Only these three directions are asserted to bisect the middle
body. No global central symmetry has been introduced.

## 3. Exact flat rounding for every nearby threshold vector

For epsilon>0 set

    A_epsilon=K+epsilon E,
    B_epsilon=B+2epsilon E,
    Khat_-1=-A_epsilon, Khat_0=B_epsilon,
    Khat_1=A_epsilon,
    Mhat_epsilon=2|A_epsilon|+|B_epsilon|.                 (7)

The reflected endpoint identity uses E=-E.
Compatibility becomes strictly feasible:

    (A_epsilon+(-A_epsilon))/2
      =(K-K)/2+epsilon E
      subset B+epsilon E
      subset int(B+2epsilon E).                           (8)

More quantitatively, E contains the Euclidean ball of radius
sqrt(2/3), so (8) has a uniform support gap at least
epsilon sqrt(2/3). This gives an actual open neighborhood of
independent fiber perturbations. The same selfweight reduction
retains all convex combinations and hence the exact integer fibers.

For any a near (1/3,1/3,1/3) with sum a_i=1, use the caps

    H_i(a)={l_i(x)-(a_i-1/3)z>=0}.                         (9)

Their margins sum to zero, so they cover all of R^3.
At z=1 they select l_i(x)>=a_i-1/3 on A_epsilon.
Reflection identifies the z=-1 trace with the opposite inequality
on that same A_epsilon. Endpoint boundary nullity gives total
endpoint contribution exactly |A_epsilon|, for every a.
The middle contribution is (6) and is independent of a because
z=0. Thus the exact full-source identity is

    muhat_epsilon(H_i(a))=Mhat_epsilon/2
                 for all i and every nearby a.             (10)

This is the needed moving-threshold baseline, proved from the
finite selected-direction symmetries rather than central symmetry.
Individual endpoint traces vary with a; their sum is what cancels.

Let alpha_epsilon=(M/Mhat_epsilon)^(1/2) and dilate all continuous
fibers by alpha_epsilon. The total mass becomes exactly M and
every transformed selected cap has mass exactly D=M/2=5/4.
At the canonical threshold a_i=1/3 the planes are unchanged.
For other thresholds their transformed equations are

    l_i(x)-alpha_epsilon(a_i-1/3)z>=0.                     (11)

The finite family tends to the original one as epsilon tends to
zero. Equations (8)--(11) give a cap-budget-flat strictification
of this nonsymmetric source.

## 4. The same physical joint escape now applies

Vary only the endpoint at z=1 from K+epsilon E to
Q(W)+epsilon E, where Q(W) is the labeled affine simplex
perturbation used in the canonical selected-star calculation.
Keep the other rounded fibers fixed. By (10), its exact global
cap increments are

    muhat_(epsilon,W)(H_i(a))-Mhat_epsilon/2
      =F_(epsilon,i)(W,a)-F_(epsilon,i)(I,a).               (12)

All pure threshold derivatives of the right side vanish at W=I.
This identity is the sole symmetry input needed by the reduced
Hessian proof; it holds here exactly.

The face-tube regularity lemma extends to the fixed ellipsoid E
without a new analytic assumption. Apply one fixed invertible
continuous linear map sending E to the Euclidean ball. It sends
Q(W) to a labeled simplex, carries the moving cap to a moving cap,
and multiplies every area by one constant determinant. The
polynomial-in-radius and C2 convergence conclusions transfer
back unchanged. Equivalently, this gives a direct proof for
ellipsoidal parallel bodies.

At epsilon=0 the original endpoint K has precisely the canonical
physical right inverse and positive joint Hessian from
candidate 30d7d56bee7b8657:

    Q=5/6,  VQ=5/12>0.

The exact-cap implicit correction and reduced second derivative
therefore apply to (12). First fix any sufficiently small positive
epsilon. Along the corrected two-sided path the sum of the
positive- and negative-time volume increments is strictly
positive for sufficiently small times. One sign gives a strict
volume gain with all three selected budgets exactly unchanged.
Choose that time so small that (8)'s open compatibility margin
is retained. Surjectivity of the nearby physical cap Jacobian
then permits a still smaller correction reducing all three
budgets strictly while preserving that strict gain.

Finally apply the already fixed dilation alpha_epsilon. The
result is an actual compatible source, arbitrarily close to (1),
with a nearby whole-space-covering three-cap group satisfying

    M_new>5/2,
    mu_new(H_i_new)<5/4 for each i=0,1,2.                  (13)

The order epsilon first, then the smaller physical motion, is
the same as in the audited rounding theorem. There is no attempt
to make a large O(t) physical move fit inside an o(t) slack.

## 5. What this extension does and does not remove

The construction removes central symmetry for one explicit actual
source, and it removes the open free-endpoint assumption because
the original midpoint constraints are active. It preserves a
finite selected family of cap budgets by exact determinant-one
reflections. It does not solve a general cap-budget balancing
problem for arbitrary sources or selected normals.

It also does not make the chosen budgets critical. For example,
at the origin the nonselected cap {2x+y<=0}, with no base tilt,
has endpoint contribution V=1/2. In B its scalar vertex values
are 1,1,-2, so its area is (2/3)^2 |B|=2/3. Its total mass is
7/6<5/4. Thus (10) does not imply that every through-origin cap
has half the mass, and no maximal-depth assertion is inferred
from this selected cover.

The exact verifier is
verify_finite_reflection_cap_flat_rounding.py.
